# Wire UI — Full Documentation

> AI-native unstyled primitives framework for React, Vue, and SolidJS. Headless, compound components with AI-integrated docs. Zero CSS — style via data-* attributes.

Wire UI provides AI-native, headless compound components for React, Vue, and SolidJS. Components handle interaction states, accessibility, and complex behaviors while shipping zero CSS. Style them with Tailwind, CSS Modules, or plain CSS — anything that supports attribute selectors. The same building blocks the components are made from are exported as hooks (React), composables (Vue), and primitives (Solid, named `createX`).

Packages: @wire-ui/react · @wire-ui/vue · @wire-ui/solid
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@wire-ui/react · https://www.npmjs.com/package/@wire-ui/vue · https://www.npmjs.com/package/@wire-ui/solid
GitHub: https://github.com/wire-ui/wire-ui

---

## Introduction

### Core Principles

**AI-native.** AI-integrated docs with llms.txt, SKILL.md, machine-readable API references, and an MCP server.

**Unstyled primitives.** No CSS shipped. No design opinions. You own the design system.

**Multi-framework.** First-class React, Vue, and SolidJS targets — identical component APIs and data attributes across all three. Hooks expose as `useX` for React and Vue; Solid follows its `createX` convention.

**State via data-* attributes.** Every interactive state (hover, focus, active, disabled, open/closed) is exposed as a data attribute — empty string when active, absent when not. Style with CSS attribute selectors.

**Compound components.** Complex widgets follow the `Component.Part` pattern. You compose the markup, control the order, and add whatever wrapper elements you need.

**Consumer-owned validation.** Form components expose `invalidType` / `invalid` and `errorMessage` props but perform no validation internally. Set the prop when your validation logic decides it's invalid — the component renders the error state.

**asChild for polymorphism.** Pass `asChild` to Button (and other components that support it) to merge all props onto your own child element — great for router links and icon buttons.

---

## Getting Started

### Installation

```bash
# React (peer dep: react >= 19, react-dom >= 19)
npm install @wire-ui/react

# Vue (peer dep: vue ^3.5)
npm install @wire-ui/vue

# SolidJS (peer dep: solid-js ^1.9)
npm install @wire-ui/solid
```

Wire UI has no production dependencies — only the matching framework peer.

### Styling Approach

Wire UI ships no CSS. All interactive state is exposed through data-* attributes. Target them with any CSS approach you prefer.

#### Tailwind CSS (v3 / v4)

Use the `data-[attr]:` modifier syntax:

```tsx
<Button className="
  px-4 py-2 rounded bg-blue-600 text-white transition-all
  data-[hover]:bg-blue-700
  data-[active]:scale-95
  data-[focus-visible]:ring-2 data-[focus-visible]:ring-offset-2
  data-[disabled]:opacity-50 data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed
">
  Submit
</Button>
```

#### Plain CSS / CSS Modules

```css
.button[data-hover]         { background: #1d4ed8; }
.button[data-active]        { transform: scale(0.95); }
.button[data-focus-visible] { outline: 2px solid #2563eb; }
.button[data-disabled]      { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }
```

### Compound Components

Complex components use the `Component.Part` pattern. You compose the markup yourself:

```tsx
import { Input } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Input.Root value={value} onChange={setValue}>
  <Input.Label>Email address</Input.Label>
  <Input.Field type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
  <Input.Error />
</Input.Root>
```

Vue and Solid expose the same shape (e.g. `<Input.Root>` / `<Input.Field>`); only the binding syntax differs.

### Validation Pattern

Wire UI components do not validate internally. You own validation:

```tsx
const [email, setEmail] = useState('')
const [invalidType, setInvalidType] = useState('')

function handleSubmit(e) {
  e.preventDefault()
  if (!email) setInvalidType('required')
  else if (!email.includes('@')) setInvalidType('email')
  else setInvalidType('')
}

<Input.Root
  value={email}
  onChange={setEmail}
  invalidType={invalidType}
  errorMessage={{
    required: 'Email is required',
    email: 'Enter a valid email address',
  }}
>
  <Input.Label>Email</Input.Label>
  <Input.Field type="email" />
  <Input.Error />
</Input.Root>
```

### TypeScript

All prop types are exported from each framework package:

```ts
// React
import type {
  ButtonProps, InputRootProps, TextareaRootProps, PasswordRootProps,
  ModalRootProps, AccordionRootProps, SearchOption, Size, Status,
} from '@wire-ui/react'

// Vue
import type { ButtonProps, InputRootProps /* … */ } from '@wire-ui/vue'

// SolidJS
import type { ButtonProps, InputRootProps /* … */ } from '@wire-ui/solid'
```

---

## Data Attributes

All interactive state is exposed through data-* attributes. An attribute is present as an empty string when active and absent when not — never "true" or "false".

```css
[data-hover]         { ... }  /* correct */
[data-hover="true"]  { ... }  /* never matches */
```

### Universal Interactive Attributes

Set by `useInteractiveState` and available on Button and any component using the hook.

| Attribute          | When present                                         |
|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| data-hover         | Mouse is over the element                            |
| data-focus-visible | Element has keyboard focus (matches :focus-visible)  |
| data-active        | Element is being pressed                             |
| data-disabled      | Element is disabled                                  |
| data-autofocus     | Element was rendered with the autoFocus prop         |

### Form Field Attributes

| Attribute    | Component                                                   | When present                              |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| data-active  | Input, Textarea, Password, NumberInput, OTP Slot, TagInput  | Field is focused                          |
| data-invalid | Input, Textarea, Password, Form.Field                       | invalidType / invalid prop is set         |
| data-success | Input, Textarea                                             | isSuccess prop is true                    |
| data-required| Form.Field                                                  | required prop is true                     |
| data-readonly| NumberInput                                                 | readOnly prop is true                     |

### State Attributes

| Attribute        | Component                                                                                                  | Values                                    |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| data-state       | Modal, Drawer, Accordion, Dropdown, Tooltip, Popover, ContextMenu, MenuBar, NavigationMenu, Combobox, Tabs | "open"/"closed", "active"/"inactive", "checked"/"unchecked" |
| data-visible     | Password.Toggle                                                                                            | Present when password is visible          |
| data-loading     | Search.Root, Skeleton                                                                                      | Present when loading                      |
| data-highlighted | Search.Item, Combobox.Item                                                                                 | Present on keyboard-focused item          |
| data-complete    | OTP.Root                                                                                                   | Present when all slots filled             |
| data-selected    | Calendar (day), TreeView                                                                                   | Present when selected                     |
| data-side        | Tooltip.Content, Popover.Content                                                                           | "top" / "right" / "bottom" / "left"       |
| data-align       | Popover.Content                                                                                            | "start" / "center" / "end"                |
| data-orientation | Tabs, ResizablePanels, Slider                                                                              | "horizontal" / "vertical"                 |
| data-dragging    | FileUpload.Dropzone                                                                                        | Present during drag-over                  |
| data-current     | Breadcrumb.Item                                                                                            | Present on current page (mirrors aria-current) |
| data-active (link)| NavigationMenu.Link                                                                                       | Present when `active` prop is true        |
| data-status      | Alert, Avatar.Image, Toast (per-toast)                                                                     | Consumer-set or component-set status      |

---

## Hooks / Composables / Primitives

React and Vue expose these as `useX`; Solid follows its `createX` naming convention. Same behaviour, same data attributes, framework-idiomatic signatures.

### State

### useControllableState

Unified state for components that can be controlled or uncontrolled — when `value` is provided the parent owns state; when omitted, state lives internally.

```tsx
import { useControllableState } from '@wire-ui/react'

function Switch({ checked, defaultChecked, onCheckedChange }) {
  const [isOn, setOn] = useControllableState({
    value: checked,
    defaultValue: defaultChecked ?? false,
    onChange: onCheckedChange,
  })
  return <button role="switch" aria-checked={isOn} onClick={() => setOn(!isOn)} />
}
```

Signature: `useControllableState({ value, defaultValue, onChange })` → `[value, setValue]` tuple. Solid: `createControllableState`.

---

### useDisclosure

Manages a boolean open/close state with stable `open`, `close`, and `toggle` handlers for modals, drawers, dropdowns.

```tsx
import { useDisclosure } from '@wire-ui/react'

function ExampleModal() {
  const { isOpen, open, close, toggle } = useDisclosure({
    defaultOpen: false,
    onOpenChange: (next) => console.log('open:', next),
  })
  return <button onClick={toggle}>{isOpen ? 'Close' : 'Open'}</button>
}
```

Signature: `useDisclosure({ defaultOpen?, onOpenChange? })` → `{ isOpen, open, close, toggle, setOpen }`. Solid: `createDisclosure`.

---

### useId

Returns a stable, SSR-safe unique id with an optional human-readable prefix; pass a `staticId` to honor a parent-provided id.

```tsx
import { useId } from '@wire-ui/react'

function Field({ id, label }) {
  const inputId = useId('field', id)
  const labelId = useId('field-label')
  return (
    <>
      <label id={labelId} htmlFor={inputId}>{label}</label>
      <input id={inputId} aria-labelledby={labelId} />
    </>
  )
}
```

Signature: `useId(prefix?, staticId?)` → `string`. Defaults `prefix` to `'wire'`. Solid: `createId`.

---

### Interaction

### useClickOutside

Fires a callback when the user clicks or taps (`click` + `touchstart`) outside a referenced element — for dismissable overlays.

```tsx
import { useRef, useState } from 'react'
import { useClickOutside } from '@wire-ui/react'

function Popover() {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(true)
  useClickOutside(ref, () => setOpen(false))
  return open ? <div ref={ref}>Click outside to close.</div> : null
}
```

Signature: `useClickOutside(ref, callback)` where callback receives the `MouseEvent | TouchEvent`. Solid: `createClickOutside` (takes an element accessor).

---

### useFocusTrap

Traps keyboard focus inside a container while `active`, cycling Tab/Shift+Tab between the first and last focusable descendants; restores focus on deactivate.

```tsx
import { useRef, useState } from 'react'
import { useFocusTrap } from '@wire-ui/react'

function Dialog() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const dialogRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  useFocusTrap(dialogRef, { active: open })
  return open ? <div ref={dialogRef} role="dialog" aria-modal="true">…</div> : null
}
```

Signature: `useFocusTrap(containerRef, { active?, returnFocus?, initialFocus? })`. Solid: `createFocusTrap`.

---

### useFocusVisible

Tracks whether focus arrived from keyboard navigation (mirrors CSS `:focus-visible`) — returns a flag plus focus handlers to spread onto the element.

```tsx
import { useFocusVisible } from '@wire-ui/react'

function FocusableButton() {
  const { isFocusVisible, focusProps } = useFocusVisible()
  return (
    <button {...focusProps} data-focus-visible={isFocusVisible ? '' : undefined}>
      Tab to me
    </button>
  )
}
```

Signature: `useFocusVisible()` → `{ isFocusVisible, focusProps: { onFocus, onBlur } }`. Solid: `createFocusVisible`.

---

### useInteractiveState

Tracks hover, keyboard-focus, and press state for any element — returns event handlers plus matching `data-hover` / `data-focus-visible` / `data-active` / `data-disabled` attributes for CSS styling.

```tsx
import { useInteractiveState } from '@wire-ui/react'

function Card({ disabled }) {
  const { handlers, dataAttributes } = useInteractiveState({ disabled })
  return (
    <div tabIndex={0} role="button" {...handlers} {...dataAttributes}
      className="data-[hover]:bg-gray-50 data-[active]:scale-95 data-[focus-visible]:ring-2">
      Card
    </div>
  )
}
```

Signature: `useInteractiveState({ disabled? })` → `{ handlers, dataAttributes, isHovered, isFocusVisible, isActive }`. Solid: `createInteractiveState`.

---

### useKeyboard

Maps keyboard events to handlers with modifier-key matching; pass tuples to require specific modifiers and opt into `preventDefault` / `stopPropagation`.

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react'
import { useKeyboard } from '@wire-ui/react'

function CommandPalette({ onSave, onClose }) {
  const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)
  useKeyboard({
    Escape: onClose,
    s: [onSave, { meta: true, preventDefault: true }],
  }, { target: inputRef, event: 'keydown' })
  return <input ref={inputRef} />
}
```

Signature: `useKeyboard(map, { target?, event?, enabled? })` where map is `Record<string, handler | [handler, options]>`. Solid: `createKeyboard`.

---

### Layout

### useFloating

Lightweight positioning for tooltips/popovers/dropdowns — computes `floatingStyles` to place a floating element on a chosen side/alignment relative to a reference, with `flip` and `shift` to stay in viewport.

```tsx
import { useRef, useState } from 'react'
import { useFloating } from '@wire-ui/react'

function Tooltip({ label, children }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const referenceRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)
  const floatingRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const { floatingStyles, side } = useFloating(referenceRef, floatingRef, {
    open, side: 'top', offset: 6,
  })
  return open ? <div ref={floatingRef} style={floatingStyles} data-side={side}>{label}</div> : null
}
```

Signature: `useFloating(referenceRef, floatingRef, { open?, side?, align?, offset?, strategy?, flip?, shift? })` → `{ x, y, side, align, strategy, floatingStyles, update }`. Solid: `createFloating`.

---

### useScrollLock

Locks document scrolling while `active`, with reference-counted nested locks and scrollbar-width padding compensation to prevent layout shift.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { useScrollLock } from '@wire-ui/react'

function Drawer() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  useScrollLock(open)
  return open ? <div role="dialog">…</div> : null
}
```

Signature: `useScrollLock(active)` — no return; lock is held while the component is mounted and `active` is true. Solid: `createScrollLock`.

---

### Observers

### useIntersectionObserver

Observes intersection of an element with a scroll container (or the viewport) and returns the latest `IntersectionObserverEntry`; set `once: true` for load-when-visible patterns.

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react'
import { useIntersectionObserver } from '@wire-ui/react'

function LazyImage({ src }) {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const entry = useIntersectionObserver(ref, { threshold: 0.1, once: true })
  const isVisible = entry?.isIntersecting ?? false
  return <div ref={ref}>{isVisible && <img src={src} alt="" />}</div>
}
```

Signature: `useIntersectionObserver(ref, { root?, rootMargin?, threshold?, once?, enabled? })` → `IntersectionObserverEntry | null`. Solid: `createIntersectionObserver`.

---

### useResizeObserver

Observes an element's content-box dimensions; optionally pass `onResize` for an imperative callback. Gracefully no-ops when `ResizeObserver` is unavailable.

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react'
import { useResizeObserver } from '@wire-ui/react'

function ResizableBox() {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const { width, height } = useResizeObserver(ref)
  return <div ref={ref}>{Math.round(width)} × {Math.round(height)}</div>
}
```

Signature: `useResizeObserver(ref, onResize?)` → `{ width, height }`. Solid: `createResizeObserver`.

---

### Utilities

### useDebounce

Debounces a reactive value (`useDebounce`) or wraps a callback into a stable debounced version (`useDebouncedCallback`) — only fires after `delay` ms of inactivity.

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
import { useDebounce } from '@wire-ui/react'

function Search() {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState('')
  const debouncedQuery = useDebounce(query, 250)
  useEffect(() => {
    if (debouncedQuery) fetch(`/api/search?q=${debouncedQuery}`)
  }, [debouncedQuery])
  return <input value={query} onChange={e => setQuery(e.target.value)} />
}
```

Signature: `useDebounce(value, delay)` → debounced value; `useDebouncedCallback(callback, delay)` → stable debounced callback that always uses the latest reference. Solid: `createDebounce` / `createDebouncedCallback`.

---

### useThrottle

Throttles a reactive value (`useThrottle`) or wraps a callback (`useThrottledCallback`) — emits at most once per `delay` ms, leading edge for callbacks.

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
import { useThrottle } from '@wire-ui/react'

function ScrollIndicator() {
  const [scrollY, setScrollY] = useState(0)
  const throttledScrollY = useThrottle(scrollY, 100)
  useEffect(() => {
    const onScroll = () => setScrollY(window.scrollY)
    window.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll)
    return () => window.removeEventListener('scroll', onScroll)
  }, [])
  return <p>{Math.round(throttledScrollY)}</p>
}
```

Signature: `useThrottle(value, delay)` → throttled value; `useThrottledCallback(callback, delay)` → leading-edge throttled callback (trailing calls dropped). Solid: `createThrottle` / `createThrottledCallback`.

---

### useMediaQuery

Returns whether a CSS media query currently matches; re-runs on change. SSR-safe (returns `false` on the server); backed by `useSyncExternalStore` in React.

```tsx
import { useMediaQuery } from '@wire-ui/react'

function ResponsiveNav() {
  const isMobile = useMediaQuery('(max-width: 640px)')
  return isMobile ? <MobileNav /> : <DesktopNav />
}
```

Signature: `useMediaQuery(query)` → `boolean`. Solid: `createMediaQuery`.

---

### useReduceMotion

Returns `true` when the OS-level `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` media query matches — thin wrapper around `useMediaQuery` for gating animations.

```tsx
import { useReduceMotion } from '@wire-ui/react'

function FadeIn({ children }) {
  const reduceMotion = useReduceMotion()
  const duration = reduceMotion ? 0 : 200
  return <div style={{ transition: `opacity ${duration}ms` }}>{children}</div>
}
```

Signature: `useReduceMotion()` → `boolean`. Solid: `createReduceMotion`.

---

### useMergedRefs

Merges multiple refs into a single callback ref so a component can keep an internal ref alongside a forwarded one (React + Solid only — Vue uses template refs directly).

```tsx
import { forwardRef, useEffect, useRef } from 'react'
import { useMergedRefs } from '@wire-ui/react'

const AutoFocusInput = forwardRef<HTMLInputElement>((props, forwardedRef) => {
  const localRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)
  const mergedRef = useMergedRefs(localRef, forwardedRef)
  useEffect(() => { localRef.current?.focus() }, [])
  return <input ref={mergedRef} {...props} />
})
```

Signature: `useMergedRefs<T>(...refs)` → `RefCallback<T>`; accepts ref objects, callback refs, or `null` / `undefined` (skipped). Solid: `createMergedRefs` (accepts ref setter functions).

---

## Components

### Layout

### Accordion

Collapsible sections. Supports `single` (one item open at a time) and `multiple` (many open at once). Controlled and uncontrolled.

```tsx
import { Accordion } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Accordion.Root type="single" collapsible defaultValue="item-1">
  <Accordion.Item value="item-1">
    <Accordion.Trigger>Section one</Accordion.Trigger>
    <Accordion.Content>Content for section one.</Accordion.Content>
  </Accordion.Item>
</Accordion.Root>
```

Props (Root): type ("single" | "multiple"), collapsible (boolean), defaultValue (string), value (string), onValueChange (fn).
Data attributes: data-state ("open" | "closed") on Item, Trigger, Content.

---

### AspectRatio

Wraps a child in a fixed width-to-height ratio using the native CSS `aspect-ratio` property.

```tsx
import { AspectRatio } from '@wire-ui/react'

<AspectRatio ratio={16 / 9} className="overflow-hidden rounded-[8px] border border-black">
  <img src="/banner.jpg" alt="" className="size-full object-cover" />
</AspectRatio>
```

Props (Root): ratio (number, default 1), ...HTMLAttributes.
Data attributes: data-ratio (always — numeric ratio value).

---

### Card

A simple unstyled container element. Pass data-color and data-size to drive design token styles.

```tsx
import { Card } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Card data-color="primary" data-size="medium" className="rounded-xl border p-6">
  Card content
</Card>
```

---

### Divider

Horizontal or vertical separator. Decorative by default (aria-hidden). Pass decorative={false} for a semantic separator.

```tsx
import { Divider } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Divider className="my-4 border-t border-gray-200" />
<Divider orientation="vertical" className="mx-4 border-l border-gray-200 h-full" />
```

Props: orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical"), decorative (boolean).

---

### List

Ordered or unordered list container. Variant attributes used as CSS hooks.

```tsx
import { List } from '@wire-ui/react'

<List.Root data-type="disc" data-size="medium" data-striped data-divider>
  <List.Item>First item</List.Item>
  <List.Item>Second item</List.Item>
</List.Root>
```

Data attributes: data-type, data-size, data-striped, data-divider on Root.

---

### ResizablePanels

Drag-to-resize panel layout with horizontal/vertical orientation, per-panel min/max constraints, and nestable groups for IDE-style splits.

```tsx
import { ResizablePanels } from '@wire-ui/react'

<ResizablePanels.Group orientation="horizontal">
  <ResizablePanels.Panel defaultSize={25} minSize={15} maxSize={50}>Sidebar</ResizablePanels.Panel>
  <ResizablePanels.Handle className="w-px bg-black" />
  <ResizablePanels.Panel defaultSize={75}>Content</ResizablePanels.Panel>
</ResizablePanels.Group>
```

Props (Group): orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical"), sizes (number[]), defaultSizes (number[]), onSizesChange.
Props (Panel): defaultSize (number), minSize (number), maxSize (number).
Props (Handle): disabled (boolean), aria-label (string).
Data attributes: data-orientation on Group/Panel/Handle, data-panel on Panel, data-handle on Handle, data-disabled on Handle.

---

### Skeleton

A loading placeholder that swaps in real children when `loading` is false; announces itself as a polite live region while loading.

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Skeleton loading={isLoading}>
  <p>Loaded content</p>
</Skeleton>

<Skeleton className="animate-pulse rounded-[8px] bg-[#e5e5e5] h-4 w-48" />
```

Props (Root): loading (boolean, default true), aria-label (string, default "Loading"), ...HTMLAttributes.
Data attributes: data-loading (always present on the placeholder).

---

### Feedback

### Alert

Dismissible alert with optional auto-dismiss timer. Status variants applied via data-status.

```tsx
import { Alert } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Alert
  data-status="success"
  className="p-4 rounded-lg data-[status=success]:bg-green-50"
  onDismiss={() => setVisible(false)}
  autoDismiss={5000}
>
  <Alert.Content>Operation completed successfully.</Alert.Content>
  <Alert.Dismiss>✕</Alert.Dismiss>
</Alert>
```

Props: onDismiss (fn), autoDismiss (number ms). Data attributes: data-status (consumer-set: "success" | "warning" | "danger").

---

### Badge

Numeric count badge. Caps display at 9+. Renders nothing when count is 0 or negative.

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Badge count={5} className="inline-flex items-center justify-center ...">
  {/* Badge renders the count */}
</Badge>
```

Props: count (number). Data attributes: data-count (raw number value).

---

### ProgressBar

Accessible progress indicator. Renders role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax.

```tsx
import { ProgressBar } from '@wire-ui/react'

<ProgressBar.Root value={65} max={100} data-size="medium"
  className="w-full h-2 bg-gray-200 rounded-full overflow-hidden">
  <ProgressBar.Fill className="h-full bg-blue-600 transition-all" />
</ProgressBar.Root>
```

Props (Root): value (number), max (number, default 100).

---

### Rating

Star rating component. Hover preview shows the prospective rating before clicking.

```tsx
import { Rating } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Rating.Root value={rating} onChange={setRating} max={5}>
  {Array.from({ length: 5 }).map((_, i) => (
    <Rating.Star key={i} index={i + 1}
      className="w-6 h-6 cursor-pointer data-[filled]:text-yellow-400 data-[hover]:text-yellow-300" />
  ))}
</Rating.Root>
```

Props (Root): value (number), onChange (fn), max (number), readOnly (boolean), disabled (boolean).
Data attributes: data-filled, data-hover on Star.

---

### Spinner

Semantic loading-indicator wrapper that provides `role="status"`, a polite live region, and a visually-hidden label around your own animated visual.

```tsx
import { Spinner } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Spinner label="Saving changes" className="inline-flex">
  <svg className="size-5 animate-spin" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none">
    <circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10" stroke="#e5e5e5" strokeWidth="2" />
    <path d="M22 12a10 10 0 0 0-10-10" stroke="black" strokeWidth="2" strokeLinecap="round" />
  </svg>
</Spinner>
```

Props (Root): label (string, default "Loading"), decorative (boolean, default true), ...HTMLAttributes.
Data attributes: none (purely semantic — uses role="status" + aria-live="polite").

---

### Forms

### Button

A native button with full interactive state tracking. Use asChild to render as any element.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Button
  className="px-4 py-2 rounded bg-blue-600 text-white
    data-[hover]:bg-blue-700
    data-[active]:scale-95
    data-[focus-visible]:ring-2
    data-[disabled]:opacity-40"
  onClick={() => handleClick()}
>
  Save changes
</Button>

// Polymorphic — renders as anchor
<Button asChild>
  <a href="/dashboard">Dashboard</a>
</Button>
```

Props: asChild (boolean), disabled (boolean), all native button props.
Data attributes: data-hover, data-focus-visible, data-active, data-disabled, data-autofocus.

---

### Calendar

Headless month calendar with controlled selection, min/max + custom date disabling, configurable week-start/locale, and render-props for day and weekday cells.

```tsx
import { Calendar } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Calendar.Root value={selected} onChange={setSelected}>
  <Calendar.Nav>
    <Calendar.PrevButton />
    <Calendar.Title />
    <Calendar.NextButton />
  </Calendar.Nav>
  <Calendar.Grid
    renderDay={(day) => <button {...day.props}>{day.dayOfMonth}</button>}
    renderWeekday={(wd) => <div>{wd.short}</div>}
  />
</Calendar.Root>
```

Props (Root): value (Date | null), defaultValue, onChange, month/defaultMonth/onMonthChange, minDate (Date), maxDate (Date), isDateDisabled ((date) => boolean), weekStartsOn (0-6), locale (string).
Data attributes (on day button): data-selected, data-today, data-outside-month, data-disabled, data-weekend.

---

### Checkbox

Multi-select checkbox group. Controlled via value: (string | number)[] and onChange.

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Checkbox.Group value={selected} onChange={setSelected}>
  <Checkbox.Item value="react">
    <Checkbox.Indicator className="w-4 h-4 border rounded data-[checked]:bg-blue-600" />
    <Checkbox.Label>React</Checkbox.Label>
  </Checkbox.Item>
  <Checkbox.Item value="vue">
    <Checkbox.Indicator className="w-4 h-4 border rounded data-[checked]:bg-blue-600" />
    <Checkbox.Label>Vue</Checkbox.Label>
  </Checkbox.Item>
</Checkbox.Group>
```

Props (Group): value (array), onChange (fn). Data attributes: data-checked on Item/Indicator when selected.

---

### Combobox

Filterable autocomplete with full keyboard navigation, ARIA listbox semantics, and a render-prop items API.

```tsx
import { Combobox } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Combobox.Root options={options}>
  <Combobox.Input placeholder="Search…" />
  <Combobox.Trigger>▾</Combobox.Trigger>
  <Combobox.Content>
    <Combobox.Items>
      {({ option, selected }) => (
        <div className="group-data-[highlighted]:bg-[#f5f5f5] group-data-[selected]:font-semibold">
          {option.label}
        </div>
      )}
    </Combobox.Items>
    <Combobox.Empty>No results</Combobox.Empty>
  </Combobox.Content>
</Combobox.Root>
```

Props (Root): options (ComboboxOption[]), value/defaultValue/onChange, inputValue/defaultInputValue/onInputChange, filter ((opt, input) => boolean), open/defaultOpen/onOpenChange, disabled (boolean).
Data attributes: data-state ("open" | "closed") on Root/Trigger/Content, data-disabled on Root/Trigger/Item, data-highlighted on Item, data-selected on Item.

---

### DatePicker

Trigger button paired with a popover Calendar; closes on selection by default and exposes a formatted value display via `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.

```tsx
import { Calendar, DatePicker } from '@wire-ui/react'

<DatePicker.Root value={date} onChange={setDate}>
  <DatePicker.Trigger>
    <DatePicker.Value placeholder="Pick a date" />
  </DatePicker.Trigger>
  <DatePicker.Content>
    <DatePicker.Calendar>
      <Calendar.Nav><Calendar.PrevButton /><Calendar.Title /><Calendar.NextButton /></Calendar.Nav>
      <Calendar.Grid renderDay={(d) => <button {...d.props}>{d.dayOfMonth}</button>} renderWeekday={(wd) => <div>{wd.short}</div>} />
    </DatePicker.Calendar>
  </DatePicker.Content>
</DatePicker.Root>
```

Props (Root): value/defaultValue/onChange (Date | null), open/defaultOpen/onOpenChange, disabled (boolean), closeOnSelect (boolean, default true), locale (string), formatOptions (Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions).
Props (Value): placeholder (ReactNode), children ((date, formatted) => ReactNode).
Data attributes: data-state ("open" | "closed") on Root/Trigger, data-disabled on Root, data-placeholder on Value when empty.

---

### FileUpload

Headless file upload combining a hidden native `<input type="file">` with a click Trigger or drag-and-drop Dropzone; validates against `accept`, `maxFiles`, and `maxSize`.

```tsx
import { FileUpload } from '@wire-ui/react'

<FileUpload.Root value={files} onChange={setFiles} accept="image/*" maxSize={2 * 1024 * 1024} multiple onReject={console.warn}>
  <FileUpload.Input />
  <FileUpload.Dropzone className="data-[dragging]:bg-[#e5e5e5]">Click or drag images here</FileUpload.Dropzone>
  <FileUpload.Items>
    {(file, i, remove) => (
      <li key={i}>{file.name}<button onClick={remove}>×</button></li>
    )}
  </FileUpload.Items>
</FileUpload.Root>
```

Props (Root): value/defaultValue (File[]), onChange, multiple (boolean), accept (string), maxFiles (number), maxSize (number, bytes), disabled (boolean), onReject (({ file, reason: "maxFiles" | "maxSize" | "accept" }[]) => void).
Data attributes: data-dragging on Dropzone during drag-over, data-disabled on Root/Dropzone/Trigger.

---

### Form

Headless form primitives that auto-wire `htmlFor`/`id`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`/`aria-required`/`disabled`, and matching `data-*` flags onto your own controls; validation is bring-your-own via the Field's `invalid` prop.

```tsx
import { Form } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Form.Root onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
  <Form.Field name="email" invalid={emailInvalid} required>
    <Form.Label>Email</Form.Label>
    <Form.Control>
      <input type="email" value={email} onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)} />
    </Form.Control>
    <Form.Description>We'll send a magic link.</Form.Description>
    <Form.Error>Please enter a valid email address.</Form.Error>
  </Form.Field>
  <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</Form.Root>
```

Props (Field): name (string), invalid (boolean), required (boolean), disabled (boolean).
Props (Label): asChild (boolean).
Props (Control): children (single ReactElement — id/name/aria-* merged onto it).
Props (Error): forceMount (boolean).
Data attributes: data-invalid, data-required, data-disabled on Field/Label/Control when the corresponding Field prop is true.

---

### Input

Compound component for text inputs. Validation is entirely consumer-controlled.

```tsx
import { Input } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Input.Root
  value={value}
  onChange={setValue}
  invalidType={invalidType}
  errorMessage={{ required: 'This field is required' }}
>
  <Input.Label>Email</Input.Label>
  <Input.Field type="email" placeholder="you@example.com"
    className="w-full border rounded px-3 py-2
      data-[active]:ring-2 data-[invalid]:border-red-500" />
  <Input.Error className="text-sm text-red-500 mt-1" />
</Input.Root>
```

Props (Root): value, onChange, invalidType (string), errorMessage (Record<string, string>), isSuccess (boolean).
Data attributes: data-active (focused), data-invalid, data-success on Field.

---

### NumberInput

Numeric input with increment/decrement buttons, min/max clamping, configurable step + precision, and full keyboard support (Arrows, PageUp/Down, Home/End). Use `null` to represent empty.

```tsx
import { NumberInput } from '@wire-ui/react'

<NumberInput.Root defaultValue={1} min={0} max={10} className="inline-flex rounded-[8px] border border-black">
  <NumberInput.Decrement className="px-3 hover:bg-[#f5f5f5]">−</NumberInput.Decrement>
  <NumberInput.Field aria-label="Quantity" className="w-16 text-center outline-none" />
  <NumberInput.Increment className="px-3 hover:bg-[#f5f5f5]">+</NumberInput.Increment>
</NumberInput.Root>
```

Props (Root): value/defaultValue (number | null), onChange, min (number), max (number), step (number, default 1), precision (number), disabled (boolean), readOnly (boolean).
Data attributes: data-disabled, data-readonly on Root; data-hover, data-focus-visible, data-active on Increment/Decrement (native `disabled` auto-set at boundaries).

---

### OTP

One-time password input. Auto-advances on type, handles Backspace, fires onComplete when all slots filled.

```tsx
import { OTP } from '@wire-ui/react'

<OTP.Root
  length={6}
  onComplete={(value) => verifyCode(value)}
  className="flex gap-2 data-[complete]:ring-2 data-[complete]:ring-green-500"
>
  {Array.from({ length: 6 }).map((_, i) => (
    <OTP.Slot key={i} index={i}
      className="w-10 h-12 border rounded text-center text-lg data-[active]:ring-2" />
  ))}
</OTP.Root>
```

Props (Root): length (number), onComplete (fn), alphanumeric (boolean).
Data attributes: data-complete on Root when all slots filled, data-active on focused Slot.

---

### Password

Password input with a built-in show/hide toggle. Validation is consumer-controlled.

```tsx
import { Password } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Password.Root value={value} onChange={setValue} invalidType={invalidType}>
  <Password.Label>Password</Password.Label>
  <Password.Field className="w-full border rounded px-3 py-2 data-[invalid]:border-red-500" />
  <Password.Toggle className="absolute right-3 top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2">
    {/* data-visible is present when password is shown */}
    Show
  </Password.Toggle>
  <Password.Error className="text-sm text-red-500 mt-1" />
</Password.Root>
```

Data attributes: data-visible on Toggle when password is visible.

### Radio

Single-selection radio group. Controlled via value and onChange.

```tsx
import { Radio } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Radio.Group value={selected} onChange={setSelected} name="size">
  {['sm', 'md', 'lg'].map((size) => (
    <Radio.Item key={size} value={size}>
      <Radio.Indicator className="w-4 h-4 rounded-full border data-[checked]:bg-blue-600" />
      <Radio.Label>{size.toUpperCase()}</Radio.Label>
    </Radio.Item>
  ))}
</Radio.Group>
```

Data attributes: data-checked on Item/Indicator when selected.

### Select

```tsx
      <Select.Item value="banana">Banana</Select.Item>

    <Select.Item value="other">Other</Select.Item>
```

### Slider

Single-value or two-thumb range slider with pointer drag and full keyboard support; horizontal/vertical and optionally inverted. (React only)

```tsx
import { Slider } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Slider defaultValue={40} min={0} max={100} step={1} aria-label="Volume" />

<Slider range defaultValue={[20, 80]} min={0} max={100} step={5} aria-label="Price range"
  className="[&_[data-part=track]]:bg-[#e5e5e5] [&_[data-part=fill]]:bg-black [&_[data-part=thumb]]:size-4 [&_[data-part=thumb]]:rounded-full [&_[data-part=thumb]]:bg-white [&_[data-part=thumb]]:border" />
```

Props: range (boolean — toggles single vs `[start, end]`), value/defaultValue (number | [number, number]), onChange, min (number, default 0), max (number, default 100), step (number, default 1), orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical"), inverted (boolean), disabled (boolean), aria-label (string).
Data attributes: data-orientation on Root, data-disabled on Root/Thumb, data-part ("track" | "fill" | "thumb") on inner spans, data-thumb-index ("0" | "1") on Thumb.

### Switch

Toggle component with a thumb element. Renders as button role="switch" with aria-checked.

```tsx
import { Switch } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Switch.Root
  checked={enabled}
  onCheckedChange={setEnabled}
  className="relative inline-flex h-6 w-11 rounded-full transition-colors
    data-[state=checked]:bg-blue-600 data-[state=unchecked]:bg-gray-300"
>
  <Switch.Thumb className="pointer-events-none block h-5 w-5 rounded-full bg-white shadow
    translate-x-0.5 transition-transform data-[state=checked]:translate-x-5.5" />
</Switch.Root>
```

Data attributes: data-state ("checked" | "unchecked") on Root and Thumb.

---

### Tag

Compact label with optional Remove button — for chips, filters, and status pills. Remove is a real `<button>` with full interactive-state tracking.

```tsx
import { Tag } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Tag.Root className="inline-flex items-center gap-1 rounded-full border border-black bg-[#f5f5f5] px-2.5 py-1 text-xs data-[disabled]:opacity-50">
  <Tag.Label>React</Tag.Label>
  <Tag.Remove onClick={() => remove('react')} className="data-[hover]:bg-[#e5e5e5] data-[focus-visible]:ring-2 data-[focus-visible]:ring-black">×</Tag.Remove>
</Tag.Root>
```

Props (Root): disabled (boolean), ...HTMLAttributes.
Props (Remove): aria-label (string, default "Remove"), ...ButtonHTMLAttributes.
Data attributes: data-disabled on Root; data-hover, data-focus-visible, data-active on Remove.

---

### TagInput

Multi-tag input where Enter or comma commits a tag and Backspace at empty input removes the last; supports validators, max-tag limits, and duplicate rejection. Tags rendered via render-prop (typically with `Tag`).

```tsx
import { TagInput, Tag } from '@wire-ui/react'

<TagInput.Root defaultValue={['react', 'tailwind']} className="flex flex-wrap gap-1.5 rounded-[8px] border border-black px-2 py-1.5 focus-within:ring-2 focus-within:ring-black">
  <TagInput.Items>
    {(tag, i, remove) => (
      <Tag.Root key={`${tag}-${i}`}>
        <Tag.Label>{tag}</Tag.Label>
        <Tag.Remove onClick={remove}>×</Tag.Remove>
      </Tag.Root>
    )}
  </TagInput.Items>
  <TagInput.Field placeholder="Add a tag…" className="flex-1 bg-transparent outline-none" />
</TagInput.Root>
```

Props (Root): value/defaultValue (string[]), onChange, disabled (boolean), maxTags (number), allowDuplicates (boolean, default false), commitKeys (string[], default `['Enter', ',']`), validate ((tag, current) => boolean).
Data attributes: data-disabled on Root (Field auto-disables when maxTags reached).

### Textarea

Same compound API as Input, renders a textarea. Controlled, uncontrolled, consumer-controlled error state.

```tsx
import { Textarea } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Textarea.Root value={value} onChange={setValue} invalidType={invalidType}>
  <Textarea.Label>Message</Textarea.Label>

    data-[active]:ring-2 data-[invalid]:border-red-500" />
  <Textarea.Error className="text-sm text-red-500 mt-1" />
</Textarea.Root>
```

### Navigation

### Breadcrumb

Semantic navigation trail (`<nav><ol>`) with current-page marking via `aria-current="page"` and a customizable separator slot.

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Breadcrumb.Root>
  <Breadcrumb.List className="flex items-center">
    <Breadcrumb.Item>
      <Breadcrumb.Link href="/" className="text-sm text-[#6b7280] hover:underline">Home</Breadcrumb.Link>
    </Breadcrumb.Item>
    <Breadcrumb.Separator className="mx-2 text-[#6b7280]">›</Breadcrumb.Separator>
    <Breadcrumb.Item current className="text-sm font-medium text-black">Profile</Breadcrumb.Item>
  </Breadcrumb.List>
</Breadcrumb.Root>
```

Props (Root): aria-label (string, default "Breadcrumb").
Props (Item): current (boolean).
Props (Link): asChild (boolean), href (string).
Props (Separator): children (ReactNode, default "/").
Data attributes: data-current on Item (also sets `aria-current="page"`); Separator gets `role="presentation"` + `aria-hidden`.

---

### MenuBar

Application-style menu bar (File/Edit/View). Click a Trigger to open its menu, then hovering other Triggers switches instantly between them.

```tsx
import { MenuBar } from '@wire-ui/react'

<MenuBar.Root className="flex items-center gap-1 rounded-[8px] border border-black p-1">
  <MenuBar.Menu value="file">
    <div className="relative">
      <MenuBar.Trigger className="rounded-[6px] px-3 py-1 text-sm hover:bg-[#f5f5f5] data-[state=open]:bg-[#f5f5f5]">File</MenuBar.Trigger>
      <MenuBar.Content className="absolute left-0 top-full z-10 mt-1 min-w-[180px] rounded-[20px] border border-black bg-white p-1">
        <MenuBar.Item onSelect={() => {}}>New</MenuBar.Item>
        <MenuBar.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Open</MenuBar.Item>
        <MenuBar.Separator />
        <MenuBar.Item>Quit</MenuBar.Item>
      </MenuBar.Content>
    </div>
  </MenuBar.Menu>
</MenuBar.Root>
```

Props (Root): value/defaultValue (string | null), onValueChange.
Props (Menu): value (string).
Props (Trigger): disabled (boolean).
Props (Item): disabled (boolean), onSelect (() => void).
Data attributes: data-state ("open" | "closed") on Menu/Trigger/Content, data-disabled on Trigger/Item, data-hover/data-active/data-focus-visible on Trigger/Item.

---

### NavigationMenu

Top navigation with hover-driven dropdown panels and configurable open/close delays; mixes plain links and dropdown triggers in a real `<nav>` landmark.

```tsx
import { NavigationMenu } from '@wire-ui/react'

<NavigationMenu.Root className="inline-flex items-center gap-1 rounded-[8px] border border-black px-2 py-1.5">
  <NavigationMenu.List className="flex items-center gap-1">
    <NavigationMenu.Item>
      <NavigationMenu.Link href="/" active className="rounded-[6px] px-3 py-1 text-sm data-[active]:bg-black data-[active]:text-white">Home</NavigationMenu.Link>
    </NavigationMenu.Item>
    <NavigationMenu.Item value="products">
      <div className="relative">
        <NavigationMenu.Trigger className="rounded-[6px] px-3 py-1 text-sm data-[state=open]:bg-[#f5f5f5]">Products</NavigationMenu.Trigger>
        <NavigationMenu.Content className="absolute left-0 top-full z-10 mt-2 min-w-[280px] rounded-[20px] border border-black bg-white p-3">
          <NavigationMenu.Link href="/design">Design</NavigationMenu.Link>
          <NavigationMenu.Link href="/develop">Develop</NavigationMenu.Link>
        </NavigationMenu.Content>
      </div>
    </NavigationMenu.Item>
  </NavigationMenu.List>
</NavigationMenu.Root>
```

Props (Root): value/defaultValue (string | null), onValueChange, delayDuration (number, default 100), skipDelayDuration (number, default 300), aria-label (string, default "Main").
Props (Item): value (string — required for dropdowns).
Props (Trigger): disabled (boolean).
Props (Link): active (boolean — adds data-active and `aria-current="page"`).
Data attributes: data-state ("open" | "closed") on Trigger/Content, data-active on Link, data-disabled on Trigger.

### Pagination

Headless page navigation. Configurable sibling/boundary counts produce a sequence of page numbers + ellipsis markers via an `Items` render-prop; Previous/Next buttons auto-disable at edges.

```tsx
import { Pagination } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Pagination.Root totalPages={10} defaultPage={1}>
  <Pagination.List className="flex items-center gap-1">
    <li><Pagination.Previous className="rounded-[8px] border border-black px-3 py-1.5 disabled:opacity-40">‹</Pagination.Previous></li>
    <Pagination.Items>
      {(item, i) => item === 'ellipsis'
        ? <Pagination.Ellipsis key={`e-${i}`} className="px-2" />
        : <Pagination.Item key={item} page={item}><span className="px-2 py-1.5 data-[active]:bg-black data-[active]:text-white">{item}</span></Pagination.Item>}
    </Pagination.Items>
    <li><Pagination.Next className="rounded-[8px] border border-black px-3 py-1.5">›</Pagination.Next></li>
  </Pagination.List>
</Pagination.Root>
```

Props (Root): totalPages (number, required), page/defaultPage (number, 1-based), onChange, siblingCount (number, default 1), boundaryCount (number, default 1).
Props (Item): page (number), disabled (boolean).
Props (Items): children ((item: number | "ellipsis", index: number) => ReactNode).
Helper: `getPaginationItems(total, current, siblings, boundaries)` returns `(number | 'ellipsis')[]`.
Data attributes: data-active on current Item (also `aria-current="page"`), data-hover/data-focus-visible/data-active on buttons.

---

### Tabs

Accessible tabs with horizontal/vertical orientation, automatic or manual activation, full keyboard navigation (Arrows, Home, End), and optional `forceMount` for state-preserving panels. (React only)

```tsx
import { Tabs } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Tabs.Root defaultValue="overview" className="w-full max-w-lg">
  <Tabs.List className="flex gap-1 border-b border-black">
    <Tabs.Trigger value="overview" className="px-4 py-2 text-sm border-b-2 border-transparent data-[state=active]:border-black data-[state=active]:font-semibold">Overview</Tabs.Trigger>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="details" className="px-4 py-2 text-sm border-b-2 border-transparent data-[state=active]:border-black">Details</Tabs.Trigger>
  </Tabs.List>
  <Tabs.Content value="overview" className="mt-4 text-sm">Overview content.</Tabs.Content>
  <Tabs.Content value="details" className="mt-4 text-sm">Details content.</Tabs.Content>
</Tabs.Root>
```

Props (Root): value/defaultValue (string), onChange, orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical"), activationMode ("automatic" | "manual", default "automatic").
Props (Trigger): value (string, required), disabled (boolean).
Props (Content): value (string, required), forceMount (boolean).
Data attributes: data-state ("active" | "inactive") on Trigger/Content, data-orientation on Root/List/Trigger/Content, data-disabled on Trigger.

---

### TreeView

Recursive tree with expandable branches, optional single/multiple selection, and full keyboard navigation; you supply `nodes` plus a `renderItem` render-prop.

```tsx
import { TreeView } from '@wire-ui/react'

<TreeView.Root
  nodes={nodes}
  defaultExpanded={['src']}
  selectionMode="single"
  selected={selected}
  onSelectionChange={setSelected}
  renderItem={(node, state) => (
    <div onClick={state.select} style={{ paddingLeft: state.level * 16 }} className="data-[selected]:bg-[#f5f5f5]">
      {state.hasChildren && (
        <button data-tree-toggle onClick={(e) => { e.stopPropagation(); state.toggle() }}>
          {state.expanded ? '▾' : '▸'}
        </button>
      )}
      <span>{node.label}</span>
    </div>
  )}
/>
```

Props (Root): nodes (TreeNode[]), expanded/defaultExpanded (string[]), onExpandedChange, selectionMode ("none" | "single" | "multiple"), selected/defaultSelected (string[]), onSelectionChange, renderItem ((node, state) => ReactNode).
TreeNode: id (string), label (ReactNode), children (TreeNode[]), disabled (boolean), data (unknown).
TreeItemState: level (number, 1-based), expanded, selected, hasChildren, disabled, toggle(), select().
Data attributes (per row): data-state ("open" | "closed") on branches, data-selected, data-disabled, data-level, data-has-children.
Note: nest the toggle button under `data-tree-toggle` and stop propagation so row-clicks select while chevron-clicks toggle.

---

### Overlays

### ContextMenu

Right-click triggered menu positioned at the cursor; portaled to `document.body`, closes on outside click, scroll, or Escape, and blocks page scroll while open.

```tsx
import { ContextMenu } from '@wire-ui/react'

<ContextMenu.Root>
  <ContextMenu.Trigger className="flex h-32 w-72 items-center justify-center rounded-[20px] border border-dashed border-black bg-[#f5f5f5]">Right-click here</ContextMenu.Trigger>
  <ContextMenu.Content className="min-w-[180px] rounded-[20px] border border-black bg-white p-1">
    <ContextMenu.Item onSelect={() => console.log('cut')} className="rounded-[8px] px-3 py-1.5 text-sm data-[focus-visible]:bg-[#f5f5f5] data-[disabled]:opacity-40">Cut</ContextMenu.Item>
    <ContextMenu.Item onSelect={() => console.log('copy')}>Copy</ContextMenu.Item>
    <ContextMenu.Separator className="my-1 h-px bg-black" />
    <ContextMenu.Item disabled>Paste</ContextMenu.Item>
  </ContextMenu.Content>
</ContextMenu.Root>
```

Props (Root): open/defaultOpen (boolean), onOpenChange, disabled (boolean).
Props (Item): disabled (boolean), onSelect (() => void).
Data attributes: data-state ("open" | "closed") on Root/Trigger/Content, data-disabled on Item, data-hover/data-active/data-focus-visible on Item.

---

### Drawer

Side-panel overlay. Same structure as Modal. Closes on overlay click or Escape key.

```tsx
import { Drawer } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Drawer.Root>
  <Drawer.Trigger>Open drawer</Drawer.Trigger>
  <Drawer.Backdrop className="fixed inset-0 bg-black/50" />
  <Drawer.Panel className="fixed inset-y-0 right-0 w-80 bg-white shadow-xl">
    <Drawer.Header>
      <Drawer.Title>Settings</Drawer.Title>
      <Drawer.Close>✕</Drawer.Close>
    </Drawer.Header>
    Panel content
  </Drawer.Panel>
</Drawer.Root>
```

Data attributes: data-state ("open" | "closed") on Panel, Backdrop.

---

### Dropdown

Trigger + menu pattern. Closes on Escape key, outside click, and menu item selection.

```tsx
import { Dropdown } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Dropdown.Root>
  <Dropdown.Trigger>Options</Dropdown.Trigger>
  <Dropdown.Menu className="absolute z-10 mt-1 rounded-lg border bg-white shadow-lg">
    <Dropdown.Item onSelect={() => handleEdit()}>Edit</Dropdown.Item>
    <Dropdown.Item onSelect={() => handleDelete()}>Delete</Dropdown.Item>
    <Dropdown.Separator className="my-1 border-t" />
    <Dropdown.Item onSelect={() => handleArchive()}>Archive</Dropdown.Item>
  </Dropdown.Menu>
</Dropdown.Root>
```

Props (Root): open (boolean), onOpenChange (fn), defaultOpen (boolean).
Data attributes: data-state ("open" | "closed") on Menu.

---

### Modal

Compound modal dialog. Renders into a portal, closes on overlay click or Escape key.

```tsx
import { Modal } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Modal.Root>
  <Modal.Trigger asChild>
    <button>Open modal</button>
  </Modal.Trigger>
  <Modal.Backdrop className="fixed inset-0 bg-black/50 data-[state=open]:opacity-100" />
  <Modal.Panel className="fixed top-1/2 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2
    bg-white rounded-xl p-6 w-full max-w-md shadow-xl">
    <Modal.Title>Confirm action</Modal.Title>
    <Modal.Description>This cannot be undone.</Modal.Description>
    <Modal.Close asChild>
      <button>Cancel</button>
    </Modal.Close>
  </Modal.Panel>
</Modal.Root>
```

Props (Root): open (boolean), onOpenChange (fn), defaultOpen (boolean).
Data attributes: data-state ("open" | "closed") on Panel, Backdrop.

---

### Popover

Floating panel anchored to a trigger; closes on outside click or Escape, supports `forceMount` for animations, and exposes `data-side`/`data-align` for position-aware styling. (React only — caller positions Content manually.)

```tsx
import { Popover } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Popover.Root className="relative inline-block">
  <Popover.Trigger className="rounded-[8px] border border-black bg-black px-4 py-2 text-sm text-white">Account</Popover.Trigger>
  <Popover.Content side="bottom" align="center" className="absolute left-0 top-full z-10 mt-2 w-72 rounded-[20px] border border-black bg-white p-4 text-sm data-[state=closed]:hidden">
    <p>Click outside or press Escape to close.</p>
    <Popover.Close className="mt-3 rounded-[8px] border border-black px-3 py-1.5">Close</Popover.Close>
  </Popover.Content>
</Popover.Root>
```

Props (Root): open/defaultOpen (boolean), onOpenChange, closeOnOutsideClick (boolean, default true), closeOnEscape (boolean, default true).
Props (Content): side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left", default "bottom"), align ("start" | "center" | "end", default "center"), forceMount (boolean).
Data attributes: data-state ("open" | "closed") on Root/Trigger/Content, data-side and data-align on Content, data-hover/data-focus-visible/data-active on Trigger/Close.

---

### Search

Search input with a dropdown results list. Keyboard navigation with Arrow keys, Enter to select, Escape to close.

```tsx
import { Search } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Search.Root
  options={results}
  onSearch={(q) => fetchResults(q)}
  onSelect={(item) => handleSelect(item)}
  loading={isLoading}
>
  <Search.Input className="w-full border rounded px-3 py-2" placeholder="Search..." />
  <Search.Dropdown className="absolute z-10 w-full bg-white border rounded-lg shadow-lg mt-1">
    <Search.Empty className="p-4 text-gray-500">No results found</Search.Empty>
    <Search.Loading className="p-4">Searching...</Search.Loading>
    {results.map((item) => (
      <Search.Item key={item.id} item={item}
        className="px-4 py-2 cursor-pointer data-[highlighted]:bg-gray-100">
        {item.label}
      </Search.Item>
    ))}
  </Search.Dropdown>
</Search.Root>
```

Data attributes: data-loading on Root, data-highlighted on the keyboard-focused Item.

---

### Toast

Imperative notification system: wrap with `Toast.Provider`, render one `Toast.Viewport` render-prop, and call `useToast().toast(...)` from anywhere. Per-toast duration (0 = persistent), auto-pause on hover/focus, and stable `status` values for styling.

```tsx
import { Toast, useToast } from '@wire-ui/react'

function App() {
  return (
    <Toast.Provider defaultDuration={4000}>
      <Trigger />
      <Toast.Viewport className="fixed bottom-4 right-4 z-50 flex flex-col gap-2">
        {(t, dismiss) => (
          <Toast.Root key={t.id} className="flex items-start gap-3 rounded-[8px] border border-black bg-white px-4 py-3 data-[status=success]:bg-[#f5f5f5]">
            <div className="flex-1">
              <Toast.Title>{t.title}</Toast.Title>
              <Toast.Description>{t.description}</Toast.Description>
            </div>
            <Toast.Close onClick={dismiss}>×</Toast.Close>
          </Toast.Root>
        )}
      </Toast.Viewport>
    </Toast.Provider>
  )
}

function Trigger() {
  const { toast } = useToast()
  return <button onClick={() => toast({ title: 'Saved', status: 'success' })}>Save</button>
}
```

Props (Provider): defaultDuration (number, default 5000).
Props (Viewport): children ((toast, dismiss) => ReactNode), ...div attrs.
Toast input: id (string — re-firing same id replaces in place), title (ReactNode), description (ReactNode), status ("default" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "info"), duration (number ms; 0 = persistent), pauseOnHover (boolean, default true), data (Record<string, unknown>).
Hook: `useToast()` returns `{ toast(input) => id, dismiss(id), toasts }`.
Data attributes: data-status ("default" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "info") on the per-toast Viewport shell.

---

### Tooltip

Hover/focus tooltip. Configurable delay and side.

```tsx
import { Tooltip } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Tooltip.Root delayDuration={200}>
  <Tooltip.Trigger asChild>
    <button>Hover me</button>
  </Tooltip.Trigger>
  <Tooltip.Content side="top"
    className="px-2 py-1 text-xs bg-gray-900 text-white rounded
      data-[state=open]:opacity-100 data-[state=closed]:opacity-0">
    This is a tooltip
  </Tooltip.Content>
</Tooltip.Root>
```

Props (Root): delayDuration (number ms), open (boolean), onOpenChange (fn).
Props (Content): side ("top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right").
Data attributes: data-state ("open" | "closed") on Content, data-side on Content.

---

### Media

### Avatar

Image with a lazy-loading fallback. Fallback renders automatically when src is empty or the image fails to load.

```tsx
import { Avatar } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Avatar.Root className="w-10 h-10 rounded-full overflow-hidden">
  <Avatar.Image src="/user.jpg" alt="Jane Doe" className="w-full h-full object-cover" />
  <Avatar.Fallback className="w-full h-full bg-gray-200 flex items-center justify-center">
    JD
  </Avatar.Fallback>
</Avatar.Root>
```

Data attributes: data-status ("loading" | "loaded" | "error") on Avatar.Image.

---

### Icon

Renders an SVG from a consumer-supplied icon map. Wire UI ships no SVG assets — you bring your own.

```tsx
import { Icon } from '@wire-ui/react'

const icons = {
  check: '<path d="M5 13l4 4L19 7" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" .../>',
}

<Icon name="check" icons={icons} size="medium" className="text-green-600" />
```

Props: name (string), icons (Record<string, string>), size ("small" | "medium" | "large").

---

### Image

Image wrapper with a loader placeholder shown until the image fires a load event.

```tsx
import { Image } from '@wire-ui/react'

<Image.Root data-position="center" className="relative overflow-hidden rounded-lg">
  <Image.Loader className="absolute inset-0 bg-gray-200 animate-pulse" />
  <Image.Img src="/photo.jpg" alt="Description" className="w-full h-full object-cover data-[loaded]:opacity-100 opacity-0" />
</Image.Root>
```

Data attributes: data-loaded on Img after successful load, data-position on Root.

---

### Timeago

Relative or formatted timestamp. In isDuration mode it updates live via setInterval.

```tsx
import { Timeago } from '@wire-ui/react'

// Relative: "3 minutes ago"
<Timeago date={new Date(Date.now() - 180000)} />

// Live countdown
<Timeago date={futureDate} isDuration />

// Formatted: "Jan 15, 2025"
<Timeago date="2025-01-15T10:30:00Z" format="MMM DD, YYYY" />
```

Props: date (Date | string | number), isDuration (boolean), format (string), updateInterval (number ms).
